declarations.name: the air
declarations.plain: The atmosphere as a holon: a column of gas whose density falls with height, read by anything that looks through it as how much light is lost along a ray and how much sunlight is scattered into it.

carrier.state: number density of air by height, and a Rayleigh scattering cross-section per wavelength. Which density profile (the 1976 standard atmosphere's layers, or an exponential fitted to it) is the evaluator's choice and is owed.

source.external: A. Bucholtz, 'Rayleigh-scattering calculations for the terrestrial atmosphere', Applied Optics 34, 2765

views.reads: the fraction of light that survives a ray, per wavelength: exp(-optical depth)

budget.quantity: numerical error of the drawn value against the SAME model's single-scattering integral evaluated exactly, after a stated display transform

views.reads: sunlight scattered into a ray, per wavelength (single scattering)

budget.quantity: numerical error of the drawn value against the SAME model's single-scattering integral evaluated exactly, after a stated display transform

declarations.regime: single scattering by air molecules only; a clear sky (no cloud, no aerosol, no ozone absorption); view rays from outside the atmosphere or from the ground; 440 to 680 nm
not_claimed: The budget is numerical: it bounds the drawing against the model, not the model against the real sky.
Multiple scattering, clouds, aerosols, refraction and ozone are outside the regime.
No weather: the profile does not change.
owed: The evaluator: the two integrals along a ray, in an engine of this repository. Nothing draws the air yet, so the renderer named here reads nothing today.
The display transform (exposure, tone map, transfer function) under which a display level is defined.
A bound certificate for each view. Until they exist the status stays catalogue and nothing is claimed of any picture.
